Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. STEP 1: No submission yet — recompute gives 'missing'\n        checks = ComplianceCheck.recompute_checks_for_target(\n            self.club, \"federation.club\"\n        )\n        self.assertTrue(checks)\n        check = my_check(checks)\n        self.assertIsNotNone(check)\n        self.assertEqual(check.status, \"missing\")\n\n        # STEP 2: Create and submit a document\n        submission = Submission.create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Insurance 2026\",\n                \"requirement_id\": self.requirement.id,\n                \"club_id\": self.club.id,\n            }\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(submission.status, \"draft\")\n\n        submission.action_submit()\n        self.assertEqual(submission.status, \"submitted\")\n\n        # Recompute → 'pending' (submitted but not yet approved)\n        checks = ComplianceCheck.recompute_checks_for_target(\n            self.club, \"federation.club\"\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(my_check(checks).status, \"pending\")\n\n        # Recompute using the most recent submission (rejected) → 'non_compliant'\n        checks = ComplianceCheck.recompute_checks_for_target(\n            self.club, \"federation.club\"\n        )\n        # Provides the full disciplinary pipeline from incident detection\nthrough case resolution to sanction enforcement.\n\n## Purpose\n\nTracks **incidents** that occur during matches, groups them into **disciplinary\ncases** for investigation, and records **sanctions** (fines, warnings) and\n**suspensions** (match bans) as outcomes. Links back to players, clubs, and\nreferees for comprehensive disciplinary records.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Players |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Matches |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.match.incident`\n\nAn event that occurred during a match that may trigger disciplinary action.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Incident title |\n| `match_id` | Many2one | The match |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Involved player |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Involved club |\n| `referee_id` | Many2one | Reporting referee |\n| `incident_type` | Selection | warning / yellow_card / red_card / misconduct / violence / admin_issue / other |\n| `minute_text` | Char | Match minute (text for flexibility) |\n| `description` | Text | What happened |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Linked disciplinary case |\n| `date_reported` | Date | When reported |\n| `reported_by_user_id` | Many2one | System user who filed it |\n| `status` | Selection | new / attached / closed |\n\n### `federation.disciplinary.case`\n\nAn investigation triggered by one or more incidents.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Case title |\n| `reference` | Char | Auto-sequence reference number |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / under_review / decided / appealed / closed |\n| `opened_on` / `decided_on` / `closed_on` | Date | Timeline |\n| `responsible_user_id` | Many2one | Case handler |\n| `incident_ids` | One2many | Related incidents |\n| `sanction_ids` | One2many | Resulting sanctions |\n| `suspension_ids` | One2many | Resulting suspensions |\n| `incident_count` / `sanction_count` / `suspension_count` | Integer | Dedicated stat counters for case shortcuts |\n| `subject_player_id` / `subject_club_id` / `subject_referee_id` | Many2one | Subject |\n| `summary` / `notes` | Text | Case details |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → under_review → decided → appealed / closed, with under-review cases allowed back to draft for corrections before a decision is recorded.\n- **Auto-numbering** via `ir.sequence`.\n- **Counter labels** use distinct technical field names so the case relation tabs and their stat counters do not trigger duplicate-label warnings during module loading.\n\n### `federation.sanction`\n\nA penalty imposed as the outcome of a disciplinary case.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Sanction title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `sanction_type` | Selection | fine / warning / ban / point_deduction / other |\n| Details |\n\n### `federation.suspension`\n\nA time-bound match ban for a player.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Suspension title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Suspended player |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Ban period |\n| `state` | Selection | active / served / overturned |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Disciplinary Staff | Can manage incidents, cases, sanctions, and suspensions |\n\n## Data Files\n\n| File | Content |\n|------|---------|\n| `data/ir_sequence.xml` | `FED-DISC-` sequence for case reference numbers |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Incident → Case linking** — Incidents can be grouped into a case for Create a second request, submit, reject → 'rejected', close → 'closed'\n\nKey invariants verified:\n- action_withdraw() only works from 'submitted'\n- action_approve() and action_reject() only work from 'submitted'\n- action_mark_implemented() only works from 'approved'\n- action_close() works from 'implemented' and 'rejected'\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom odoo.exceptions import ValidationError\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\nfrom odoo.addons.sports_federation_governance.workflow_states import (\n    OVERRIDE_REQUEST_STATE_APPROVED,\n    OVERRIDE_REQUEST_STATE_CLOSED,\n    OVERRIDE_REQUEST_STATE_DRAFT,\n    OVERRIDE_REQUEST_STATE_IMPLEMENTED,\n    OVERRIDE_REQUEST_STATE_REJECTED,\n    OVERRIDE_REQUEST_STATE_SUBMITTED,\n)\n\n\nclass TestTourGovernanceOverride(TransactionCase):\n    \"\"\"T-11: Governance override request lifecycle tour.\"\"\"\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n\n        # Minimal target record — tournament participant would be ideal,\n        # but we just need any real record ID.   {"content": "**Repository Summary**\n- **Purpose**: Odoo 19 custom addons to manage a sports federation (clubs, teams, seasons, tournaments, rules, officiating, rosters, results, public site, reporting).\n- **Location**: All addons live under the `odoo/` folder as individual modules prefixed with `sports_federation_`.\n-- **Primary docs**: See [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1), [odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md#L1), and the Workflows in [odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md](odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md#L1).\n\n**Architecture & Patterns**\n- **Module split**: `sports_federation_base` (master data), `sports_federation_tournament` (tournaments, matches, participants), `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (service/wizards), plus domain modules (`people`, `rules`, `officiating`, `rosters`, `result_control`, `public_site`, `reporting`, `finance_bridge`, `venues`, `discipline`, `standings`, ...).\n- **Model naming**: Domain models use the `federation.` prefix (e.g. `federation.player`, `federation.match`).\n- **Common patterns**: `ir.sequence` for identifiers, `state` selection fields for workflows, wizards for batch operations (under `wizards/`), `controllers/` for portal/website endpoints, and `security/` for groups/record rules/ACLs.\n\n**Key Files & Where To Look**\n- **High-level context**: [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1)\n- **Technical architecture**: [odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md#L1)\n-- **Workflows (authoritative behavioural spec)**: [odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md](odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md#L1) and the other files inside `odoo/_workflows`.\n- **Module READMEs**: each module may have a `README.md` under `odoo/<module>/README.md` with implementation notes and expectations.\n-- **Install logs / historical notes**: `_logs/` contains installation and setup notes per module.\n\n**Development Guidelines (how to implement changes)**\n- **Add/modify a model**: create/modify `models/*.py`, export package in `models/__init__.py`, add access rules in `security/ir.model.access.csv`, add any initial `data/*.xml` and register them in `__manifest__.py` `data` or `demo` lists, add views in `views/*.xml`, update `menu_items.xml` as needed, and add tests under `tests/`.\n- **Add a wizard or service**: put transient models under `wizards/` and views under `views/` (manifest `data`), keep service logic in modules like `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (no persistent models if not required).\n- **Add a controller / portal flow**: use `controllers/` and add templates under `views/` or `templates/`; respect portal record rules (see `sports_federation_portal`).\n- **Security**: always add or update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` groups/rules for new models or new endpoints.\n- **Manifest hygiene**: update `__manifest__.py` `depends`, `data`, and `version` fields when introducing DB changes or new data files.\n\n**Testing & Local Run**\n- **Where tests live**: `odoo/<module>/tests/` when present (some modules include unit/functional tests).\n- **Run module tests**: use the Odoo test runner for module-level tests (e.g. `odoo-bin -d <db> -i <module> --test-enable`) or your established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state transitions).\n\n**PR Checklist (required before merge)**\n- **Tests**: Add/adjust tests covering the new behaviour.\n- **Security**: Update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and add group/record-rule XML if necessary.\n- **Manifest**: Add new data files to `__manifest__.py` `data` list and ensure `depends` are correct.\n-- **Docs**: Update or add a short README in the module and, if behaviour changes, update the relevant `odoo/_workflows` file.\n- **Small, focused commits**: Prefer atomic commits (one logical change per commit) and descriptive commit messages.\n\n**How Copilot Should Help (recommended prompts & behaviour)**\n- **Primary rule**: Prefer conservative, minimal changes that keep module boundaries intact. Avoid touching unrelated modules unless absolutely required and explain why.\n- **When asked to implement a model change**: return a plan and a single patch that includes: the `models/<file>.py` change, `models/__init__.py` export, `security/ir.model.access.csv` entry, `views/*.xml` (if UI), `__manifest__.py` update, and a new test under `tests/` that exercises the main logic.\n- **When asked to add a wizard or generator**: create a transient model in `wizards/`, a wizard view, and a small deterministic example in tests that demonstrates expected output (e.g. round-robin schedule for 4 participants).\n- **When asked about business rules or workflows**: consult and reference the Workflow docs in `odoo/_workflows` and the `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` to ensure behaviour matches the documented flows.\n\n**Example prompts you can give Copilot in this repo**\n- **Add a model**: \"Add a new persistent model `federation.referee` with fields `name`, `certification_level`, `active`; add ACLs, a basic tree/form view, and unit tests. Show me the patch with files changed.\"\n- **Create a wizard**: \"Create a `round_robin_wizard` that generates matches for a stage; include wizard model, view, manifest update, and a unit test verifying match count for 4 teams.\"\n- **Fix workflow behaviour**: \"Investigate why standings recompute includes contested results; propose a minimal fix and tests to prevent contested results from being counted.\"\n\n**Notes & Expectations**\n- **Authoritative sources**: the `_workflows` documents and `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` are the source of truth for business behaviour—use them before changing workflows.\n- **Keep modules decoupled**: the architecture intentionally separates `base`, `tournament`, and the `competition_engine` service; prefer adding features in the appropriate module.\n- **Ask clarifying questions**: if a requested feature impacts tournament rules, scheduling, or publication flows, ask which workflow (`_workflows/*.md`) should govern the behaviour.\n\n**Documentation Maintenance (required)**\n\n- **Always update docs**: For any code, data model, view, workflow, or behaviour change, update the relevant documentation files in this repository as part of the same change set (or in a linked follow-up PR).   {"content": "# Competition Engine\n\nThis implementation provides role-owned capabilities and explicit handovers for competition planning and operations.\n\n## Addons\n\n1. `sports_federation_competition_core`: identity, roles, lifecycle and events.\n2. `sports_federation_registration`: application queue and finalized participant sets.\n3. `sports_federation_format`: versioned logical structures and fixtures.\n4. `sports_federation_calendar`: physical match days, round allocations and capacity.\n5. `sports_federation_scheduling`: one-way fixture-to-slot assignments, pure validation and deterministic proposals.\n6. `sports_federation_schedule_approval`: independent review and immutable publication snapshots.\n7. `sports_federation_matchday`: live operational control and incidents.\n\n## Required handovers\n\nRegistration finalizes a participant set. Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

  {"content": "# ADR-0002: Reporting SQL Views\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nFederation reporting combines finance, standings, compliance, notification, planning, and workflow data across multiple addons. Rebuilding those joins in controllers or repeated ORM loops would duplicate logic and create unpredictable performance.\n\n## Decision\n\nOperational and planning projections remain read-only analytical models backed by PostgreSQL views when their data is naturally cross-module or aggregation-heavy.\n\n- SQL-backed report models use `_auto = False`.\n- View definitions are recreated deterministically from `init()` or the repository's approved view helper.\n- Controllers and exports consume report models instead of embedding substantial SQL or cross-module aggregation logic.\n- Report models are read-only and must not masquerade as writable business records.\n- Heavy reports retain query budgets, representative fixtures, and performance watchpoints.\n- SQL view changes are upgrade-sensitive and require migration review evidence.\n- A normal stored Odoo model is preferred when the data has its own lifecycle or must be edited.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Cross-module reporting logic remains centralized.\n- Export and operator surfaces share the same projection semantics.\n- View dependencies and upgrade order require explicit review.\n- Maintainers must preserve query plans, migration safety, and read-only behavior.\n", "content_length": 1514, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0002-reporting-sql-views.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "ef36c1653fd664b1b66d727fab316472e1dd05aad0b7e71a28d0f01cd5a889ad", "size_bytes": 1514}
  {"content": "# ADR-0003: Public Route Ownership\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nPublic tournament pages, feeds, calendars, registration entry points, and compatibility aliases can collide when several addons define overlapping controllers. Numeric legacy routes also create ambiguity about the canonical public contract.\n\n## Decision\n\n- `/competitions` and `/competitions/<edition-slug>` are the canonical public page routes.\n- Tournament-named page routes are compatibility redirects only.\n\nPublic route ownership is tournament-first and module-explicit:\n\n- `sports_federation_public_site` owns canonical public competition pages and match-day publication views; legacy tournament feeds and calendars remain compatibility contracts.\n- Slug-first routes are canonical for new consumers.\n- Numeric and competition-named routes may remain only as documented compatibility aliases with an owner and review date.\n- Public reads enforce applicable publication controls such as `website_published`, `show_public_results`, and `show_public_standings`.\n- Public write entry points use a model-owned request boundary and must not broaden portal or backend privileges.\n- Route inventory, OpenAPI contracts, compatibility notes, and smoke coverage are part of the ownership boundary.\n- Duplicate or shadow public controllers are removed rather than kept as silent fallbacks.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Controller precedence and deprecation become reviewable.\n- New public surfaces must update route and contract documentation in the same change.\n- Compatibility routes carry an explicit maintenance cost and sunset decision.\n- Publication defaults remain deny-by-default.\n", "content_length": 1753, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0003-public-route-ownership.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "8f2952d166f7cf414b532edcbbe59159565833ea88c150bdc2b4a5248d639a7d", "size_bytes": 1753}

  ;;\n    *)\n      return 1\n      ;;\n  esac\n}\n\nfor arg in \"$@\"; do\n  case \"$arg\" in\n    --list-suites)\n      list_suites\n      exit 0\n      ;;\n    --help|-h)\n      usage\n      exit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nMODULES=()\nSUITES=()\nFRONTEND_MODULES=()\nCUSTOM_TEST_TAGS=\"\"\nREQUIRE_POST_TESTS=0\nKEEP=false\nKEEP_ON_FAILURE=false\nFRONTEND_MODE=false\nAFFECTED_FROM=\"\"\nINCLUDE_DEPENDENTS=false\nwhile [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo \"Missing value for $1\" >&2; usage >&2; exit 1; }\n      CUSTOM_TEST_TAGS=\"$2\"\n      shift 2\n      ;;\n    --require-post-tests)\n      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo \"Missing exit 0\n      ;;\n    --keep|-k)\n      KEEP=true\n      shift\n      ;;\n    --keep-on-failure)\n      KEEP_ON_FAILURE=true\n      shift\n      ;;\n    *)\n      echo \"Unknown option: $1\" >&2\n - {"content": "\"\"\"Tour T-10: Compliance — Document Submission, Approval, and Compliance Check\n\nWalks the compliance lifecycle:\n  1. Define a document requirement for clubs\n  2. Create a draft submission and submit it\n  3. Approve the submission → 'approved'\n  4. Recompute compliance checks → entity is 'compliant'\n  5. Reject a second submission → 'rejected' → compliance check is 'non_compliant'\n  6. Re-submit and re-approve → back to 'compliant'\n\nKey invariants verified:\n- Submission states: draft → submitted → approved / rejected\n- recompute_checks_for_target() reflects current submission status\n- Approved submission → 'compliant'; rejected → 'non_compliant'\n- Missing submission → 'missing'\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\n\nclass TestTourCompliance(TransactionCase):\n    \"\"\"T-10: Compliance document submission and check lifecycle tour.\"\"\"\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n\n        cls.club = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Compliance Tour Club\", \"code\": \"COMPL\"}\n        )\n\n        cls.requirement = cls.env[\"federation.document.requirement\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Club Insurance Certificate\",\n                \"code\": \"TOUR_INS\",\n                \"target_model\": \"federation.club\",\n                \"required_for_all\": True,\n                \"requires_expiry_date\": False,\n            }\n        )\n\n    def test_compliance_full_lifecycle(self):\n        \"\"\"Compliance: submit → approve → recompute; reject → non_compliant; re-approve.\"\"\"\n        ComplianceCheck = self.env[\"federation.compliance.check\"]\n        Submission = self.env[\"federation.document.submission\"]\n\n        def my_check(checks):\n            \"\"\"Return the check for our test requirement (avoids cross-class interference).\"\"\"\n            return next(\n                (c for c in checks if c.requirement_id.id == self.requirement.id), None\n            )\n\n        # STEP 1: No submission yet — recompute gives 'missing'\n        checks = ComplianceCheck.recompute_checks_for_target(\n            self.club, \"federation.club\"\n        )\n        self.assertTrue(checks)\n        check = my_check(checks)\n        self.assertIsNotNone(check)\n        self.assertEqual(check.status, \"missing\")\n\n        # STEP 2: Create and submit a document\n        submission = Submission.create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Insurance 2026\",\n                \"requirement_id\": self.requirement.id,\n                \"club_id\": self.club.id,\n            }\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(submission.status, \"draft\")\n\n        submission.action_submit()\n        self.assertEqual(submission.status, \"submitted\")\n\n        # Recompute → 'pending' (submitted but not yet approved)\n        checks = ComplianceCheck.recompute_checks_for_target(\n            self.club, \"federation.club\"\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(my_check(checks).status, \"pending\")\n\n        # Install the module with demo data enabled in Odoo.\n2. Open core workflows from tournament setup through match completion.\n3. Reset by recreating the database when you need a fresh deterministic dataset.\n\nScope and constraints\n- This module is for non-production environments.\n- Demo records prioritize workflow coverage over real-world data volume.\n- The seeded Spring Cup intentionally omits category and gender restrictions\n  because its participant fixture demonstrates senior, youth, and women's\n  teams in one navigable competition.\n- Data is versioned with the addon and intended to stay reproducible across installs.\n\nValidation checklist\n- Module installs without additional manual data steps.\n- Tournament, roster, and standings flows are navigable from seeded records.\n- Portal/public pages can render at least one realistic competition storyline.\n", "content_length": 1334, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_demo/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "594975346f47ebf5292b643f878af9c59744050d2d522955fb288c25ba80ba26", "size_bytes": 1334}

Provides the full disciplinary pipeline from incident detection\nthrough case resolution to sanction enforcement.\n\n## Purpose\n\nTracks **incidents** that occur during matches, groups them into **disciplinary\ncases** for investigation, and records **sanctions** (fines, warnings) and\n**suspensions** (match bans) as outcomes. `sports_federation_people` | Players |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Matches |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.match.incident`\n\nAn event that occurred during a match that may trigger disciplinary action.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Incident title |\n| `match_id` | Many2one | The match |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Involved player |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Involved club |\n| `referee_id` | Many2one | Reporting referee |\n| `incident_type` | Selection | warning / yellow_card / red_card / misconduct / violence / admin_issue / other |\n| `minute_text` | Char | Match minute (text for flexibility) |\n| `description` | Text | What happened |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Linked disciplinary case |\n| `date_reported` | Date | When reported |\n| `reported_by_user_id` | Many2one | System user who filed it |\n| `status` | Selection | new / attached / closed |\n\n### `federation.disciplinary.case`\n\nAn investigation triggered by one or more incidents.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Case title |\n| `reference` | Char | Auto-sequence reference number |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / under_review / decided / appealed / closed |\n| `opened_on` / `decided_on` / `closed_on` | Date | Timeline |\n| `responsible_user_id` | Many2one | Case handler |\n| `incident_ids` | One2many | Related incidents |\n| `sanction_ids` | One2many | Resulting sanctions |\n| `suspension_ids` | One2many | Resulting suspensions |\n| `incident_count` / `sanction_count` / `suspension_count` | Integer | Dedicated stat counters for case shortcuts |\n| `subject_player_id` / `subject_club_id` / `subject_referee_id` | Many2one | Subject |\n| `summary` / `notes` | Text | Case details |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → under_review → decided → appealed / closed, with under-review cases allowed back to draft for corrections before a decision is recorded.\n- **Auto-numbering** via `ir.sequence`.\n- **Counter labels** use distinct technical field names so the case relation tabs and their stat counters do not trigger duplicate-label warnings during module loading.\n\n### `federation.sanction`\n\nA penalty imposed as the outcome of a disciplinary case.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Sanction title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `sanction_type` | Selection | fine / warning / ban / point_deduction / other |\n| Details |\n\n### `federation.suspension`\n\nA time-bound match ban for a player.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Suspension title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Suspended player |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Ban period |\n| `state` | Selection | active / served / overturned |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Disciplinary Staff | Can manage incidents, cases, sanctions, and suspensions |\n\n## Data Files\n\n| File | Content |\n|------|---------|\n| `data/ir_sequence.xml` | `FED-DISC-` sequence for case reference numbers |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Incident → Case linking** — Incidents can be grouped into a case for reporting).\n- **Location**: All addons live under the `odoo/` folder as individual modules prefixed with `sports_federation_`.\n-- **Primary docs**: See [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1), Patterns**\n- **Module split**: `sports_federation_base` (master data), `sports_federation_tournament` (tournaments, matches, participants), `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (service/wizards), plus domain modules (`people`, `rules`, `officiating`, `rosters`, `result_control`, `public_site`, `reporting`, `finance_bridge`, `venues`, `discipline`, `standings`, ...).\n- **Model naming**: Domain models use the `federation.` prefix (e.g. `federation.player`, `federation.match`).\n- **Common patterns**: `ir.sequence` for identifiers, `state` selection fields for workflows, wizards for batch operations (under `wizards/`), `controllers/` for portal/website endpoints, and `security/` for groups/record rules/ACLs.\n\n**Key Files & Where To Look**\n- **High-level context**: [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1)\n- **Technical architecture**: [odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md#L1)\n-- **Workflows (authoritative behavioural spec)**: [odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md](odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md#L1) and the other files inside `odoo/_workflows`.\n- **Module READMEs**: each module may have a `README.md` under `odoo/<module>/README.md` with implementation notes and expectations.\n-- **Install logs / historical notes**: `_logs/` contains installation and setup notes per module.\n\n**Development Guidelines (how to implement changes)**\n- **Add/modify a model**: create/modify `models/*.py`, export package in `models/__init__.py`, add access rules in `security/ir.model.access.csv`, add any initial `data/*.xml` and register them in `__manifest__.py` `data` or `demo` lists, add views in `views/*.xml`, update `menu_items.xml` as needed, and add tests under `tests/`.\n- **Add a wizard or service**: put transient models under `wizards/` and views under `views/` (manifest `data`), keep service logic in modules like `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (no persistent models if not required).\n- **Add a controller / portal flow**: use `controllers/` and add templates under `views/` or `templates/`; respect portal record rules (see `sports_federation_portal`).\n- **Security**: always add or update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` groups/rules for new models or new endpoints.\n- **Manifest hygiene**: update `__manifest__.py` `depends`, `data`, and `version` fields when introducing DB changes or new data files.\n\n**Testing & Local Run**\n- **Where tests live**: `odoo/<module>/tests/` when present (some modules include unit/functional tests).\n- **Run module tests**: use the Odoo test runner for module-level tests (e.g. `odoo-bin -d <db> -i <module> --test-enable`) or your established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state  {"content": "# Competition Engine\n\nThis implementation provides role-owned capabilities and explicit handovers for competition planning and operations.\n\n## Addons\n\n1. `sports_federation_competition_core`: identity, roles, lifecycle and events.\n2. `sports_federation_registration`: application queue and finalized participant sets.\n3. `sports_federation_format`: versioned logical structures and fixtures.\n4. `sports_federation_calendar`: physical match days, round allocations and capacity.\n5. `sports_federation_scheduling`: one-way fixture-to-slot assignments, pure validation and deterministic proposals.\n6. `sports_federation_schedule_approval`: independent review and immutable publication snapshots.\n7. `sports_federation_matchday`: live operational control and incidents.\n\n## Required handovers\n\nRegistration finalizes a participant set. Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

 {"content": "# ADR-0002: Reporting SQL Views\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nFederation reporting combines finance, standings, compliance, notification, planning, and workflow data across multiple addons. Rebuilding those joins in controllers or repeated ORM loops would duplicate logic and create unpredictable performance.\n\n## Decision\n\nOperational and planning projections remain read-only analytical models backed by PostgreSQL views when their data is naturally cross-module or aggregation-heavy.\n\n- SQL-backed report models use `_auto = False`.\n- View definitions are recreated deterministically from `init()` or the repository's approved view helper.\n- Controllers and exports consume report models instead of embedding substantial SQL or cross-module aggregation logic.\n- Report models are read-only and must not masquerade as writable business records.\n- Heavy reports retain query budgets, representative fixtures, and performance watchpoints.\n- SQL view changes are upgrade-sensitive and require migration review evidence.\n- A normal stored Odoo model is preferred when the data has its own lifecycle or must be edited.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Cross-module reporting logic remains centralized.\n- Export and operator surfaces share the same projection semantics.\n- View dependencies and upgrade order require explicit review.\n- Maintainers must preserve query plans, migration safety, and read-only behavior.\n", "content_length": 1514, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0002-reporting-sql-views.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "ef36c1653fd664b1b66d727fab316472e1dd05aad0b7e71a28d0f01cd5a889ad", "size_bytes": 1514}
 {"content": "# ADR-0003: Public Route Ownership\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nPublic tournament pages, feeds, calendars, registration entry points, and compatibility aliases can collide when several addons define overlapping controllers. Numeric legacy routes also create ambiguity about the canonical public contract.\n\n## Decision\n\n- `/competitions` and `/competitions/<edition-slug>` are the canonical public page routes.\n- Tournament-named page routes are compatibility redirects only.\n\nPublic route ownership is tournament-first and module-explicit:\n\n- `sports_federation_public_site` owns canonical public competition pages and match-day publication views; legacy tournament feeds and calendars remain compatibility contracts.\n- Slug-first routes are canonical for new consumers.\n- Numeric and competition-named routes may remain only as documented compatibility aliases with an owner and review date.\n- Public reads enforce applicable publication controls such as `website_published`, `show_public_results`, and `show_public_standings`.\n- Public write entry points use a model-owned request boundary and must not broaden portal or backend privileges.\n- Route inventory, OpenAPI contracts, compatibility notes, and smoke coverage are part of the ownership boundary.\n- Duplicate or shadow public controllers are removed rather than kept as silent fallbacks.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Controller precedence and deprecation become reviewable.\n- New public surfaces must update route and contract documentation in the same change.\n- Compatibility routes carry an explicit maintenance cost and sunset decision.\n- Publication defaults remain deny-by-default.\n", "content_length": 1753, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0003-public-route-ownership.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "8f2952d166f7cf414b532edcbbe59159565833ea88c150bdc2b4a5248d639a7d", "size_bytes": 1753}

 {"content": "# Sports Federation Discipline\n\nIncident reporting, disciplinary case management, sanctions, and player\nsuspensions. Provides the full disciplinary pipeline from incident detection\nthrough case resolution to sanction enforcement.\n\n## Purpose\n\nTracks **incidents** that occur during matches, groups them into **disciplinary\ncases** for investigation, and records **sanctions** (fines, warnings) and\n**suspensions** (match bans) as outcomes. Links back to players, clubs, and\nreferees for comprehensive disciplinary records.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Players |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Matches |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.match.incident`\n\nAn event that occurred during a match that may trigger disciplinary action.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Incident title |\n| `match_id` | Many2one | The match |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Involved player |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Involved club |\n| `referee_id` | Many2one | Reporting referee |\n| `incident_type` | Selection | warning / yellow_card / red_card / misconduct / violence / admin_issue / other |\n| `minute_text` | Char | Match minute (text for flexibility) |\n| `description` | Text | What happened |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Linked disciplinary case |\n| `date_reported` | Date | When reported |\n| `reported_by_user_id` | Many2one | System user who filed it |\n| `status` | Selection | new / attached / closed |\n\n### `federation.disciplinary.case`\n\nAn investigation triggered by one or more incidents.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Case title |\n| `reference` | Char | Auto-sequence reference number |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / under_review / decided / appealed / closed |\n| `opened_on` / `decided_on` / `closed_on` | Date | Timeline |\n| `responsible_user_id` | Many2one | Case handler |\n| `incident_ids` | One2many | Related incidents |\n| `sanction_ids` | One2many | Resulting sanctions |\n| `suspension_ids` | One2many | Resulting suspensions |\n| `incident_count` / `sanction_count` / `suspension_count` | Integer | Dedicated stat counters for case shortcuts |\n| `subject_player_id` / `subject_club_id` / `subject_referee_id` | Many2one | Subject |\n| `summary` / `notes` | Text | Case details |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → under_review → decided → appealed / closed, with under-review cases allowed back to draft for corrections before a decision is recorded.\n- **Auto-numbering** via `ir.sequence`.\n- **Counter labels** use distinct technical field names so the case relation tabs and their stat counters do not trigger duplicate-label warnings during module loading.\n\n### `federation.sanction`\n\nA penalty imposed as the outcome of a disciplinary case.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Sanction title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `sanction_type` | Selection | fine / warning / ban / point_deduction / other |\n| `player_id` / `club_id` / `referee_id` | Many2one | Who is sanctioned |\n| `amount` / `currency_id` | Monetary | For fines |\n| `effective_date` | Date | When it takes effect |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n### `federation.suspension`\n\nA time-bound match ban for a player.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Suspension title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Suspended player |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Ban period |\n| `state` | Selection | active / served / overturned |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Disciplinary Staff | Can manage incidents, cases, sanctions, and suspensions |\n\n## Data Files\n\n| File | Content |\n|------|---------|\n| `data/ir_sequence.xml` | `FED-DISC-` sequence for case reference numbers |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Incident → Case linking** — Incidents can be grouped into a case for joint handling.\n2. **Case lifecycle** — draft → under_review → decided → appealed / closed with date tracking, and under-review cases can be reopened to draft before a decision is recorded.\n3. **Multiple outcomes** — A single case can produce multiple sanctions and suspensions.\n4. **Player integration** — Inherited views add discipline tabs to player forms.\n5. **Match integration** — Inherited views add incident lists to match forms.\n6. **Finance bridge integration** — When `sports_federation_finance_bridge` is installed,\n   sanctions of type `fine` automatically create
